meta.environment: *fill* — CICS region with transient-data queue CSSL defined
meta.author: modernizeX

cases.mid: 機能・業務フロー (Function / business flow)
cases.name: End-to-end: a failing online program invokes the handler and the task abends after the failure is logged
cases.precondition: F-STD. The CICS log queue CSSL is defined; the caller runs under a CICS task and has hit an unrecoverable error.
cases.steps:
1. From the failing online program, invoke the handler passing the abend-parameter area (values in Test data)
2. Observe the CICS log queue CSSL
3. Observe the task outcome
cases.data: F-STD: program=OCTRANV, paragraph=2100-READ-TRANSACT, resp=12, reas=0, detail=TRANSACTION FILE READ FAILED - KEY 0000000123456
cases.expected: One diagnostic line is written to the CSSL queue, then the task is abended with code OABN and a transaction dump. The handler runs the log-then-abend sequence in one linear path with no branching.
cases.remark: EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('OUABND') COMMAREA(KABND-PARM) · 0000-MAIN L21-40 · STRING → WRITEQ TD CSSL → EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE(WS-ABCODE='OABN')

cases.mid: 計算・編集ロジック (Calculation / editing logic)
cases.name: Diagnostic line assembly — fixed labels and separators are concatenated in a fixed order
cases.steps:
1. Invoke the handler with the program name, paragraph name and detail text from Test data
2. Read back the line written to the CSSL queue
cases.data: Inputs — program=OCTRANV, paragraph=2100-READ-TRANSACT, detail=TRANSACTION FILE READ FAILED - KEY 0000000123456. Expected line (CSSL): ABEND IN OCTRANV  AT 2100-READ-TRANSACT           - TRANSACTION FILE READ FAILED - KEY 0000000123456
cases.expected: The line is the fixed text 「ABEND IN 」, then the program name, then 「 AT 」, then the paragraph name, then 「 - 」, then the detail text — each value copied at its full field width (program 8, paragraph 30). The concatenated result equals the 'Expected line' in Test data.
cases.remark: STRING 'ABEND IN' DELIMITED SIZE KA-PROGRAM ' AT ' KA-PARAGRAPH ' - ' KA-DETAIL INTO WS-ABEND-MSG · L22-29

cases.name: Diagnostic line is written to the CSSL log queue at a fixed length of 120 bytes
cases.steps:
1. Invoke the handler under F-STD
2. Inspect the record appended to the CSSL queue and its length
cases.data: F-STD. CSSL record length = 120 bytes (fixed, independent of content).
cases.expected: Exactly one record is appended to the CSSL transient-data queue. The record is 120 bytes long regardless of how much of the detail was supplied — the length is fixed at the size of the diagnostic-line buffer (120).
cases.remark: WRITEQ TD QUEUE('CSSL') FROM(WS-ABEND-MSG) LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-ABEND-MSG)=120 · L30-35

cases.name: Content pass-through — a different failing site produces the correspondingly different log line
cases.precondition: F-STD, except the caller supplies a different failing program, paragraph and detail (see Test data).
cases.steps:
1. Invoke the handler with the second failing site from Test data
2. Read the line on the CSSL queue
cases.data: Inputs — program=OCBILLP, paragraph=3200-POST-PAYMENT, detail=BILL PAYMENT AMOUNT OVER LIMIT. Expected line (CSSL): ABEND IN OCBILLP  AT 3200-POST-PAYMENT            - BILL PAYMENT AMOUNT OVER LIMIT
cases.expected: The logged line carries the new program, paragraph and detail values unchanged — the handler copies whatever the caller supplies (no transformation, no fixed content of its own beyond the 'ABEND IN' / 'AT' / '-' labels). The result equals the 'Expected line' in Test data.
cases.remark: Same 0000-MAIN path, different COMMAREA values — demonstrates value pass-through (no branch drives content)

cases.name: Response and reason codes supplied in the parameter area are not written to the log line
cases.precondition: F-STD with non-zero response and reason codes supplied (resp=12, reas=8).
cases.steps:
1. Invoke the handler under F-STD with resp=12 and reas=8
2. Inspect the line on the CSSL queue for the numeric response/reason codes
cases.data: resp=12 (NOTFND), reas=8. Expected: the line contains program/paragraph/detail only; '12' and '8' do not appear.
cases.expected: The diagnostic line contains only the program name, paragraph name and detail text. The response code 12 and reason code 8 are absent from the line — the handler does not include them, so a tester must not expect the response/reason numbers in the log.
cases.remark: KA-RESP-CD / KA-REAS-CD are in COMMAREA (binary COMP) but NOT referenced by the STRING — design §5.1 lists them, source omits them

cases.mid: データ整合性・冪等性 (Data integrity / idempotency)
cases.name: One log line and one abend per invocation — repeated calls from different tasks each log independently
cases.precondition: F-STD. Two separate failing tasks each invoke the handler.
cases.steps:
1. Task A invokes the handler under F-STD
2. Task B invokes the handler with a different failing site
3. Inspect the CSSL queue and both task outcomes
cases.data: Two invocations; expect two appended records on CSSL (one per call) and two abends with code OABN.
cases.expected: Each invocation appends exactly one record to the append-only CSSL queue and abends its own task with code OABN. The two lines coexist in call order; neither call overwrites the other. Re-running the same failing input yields an identical line (the handler holds no state between calls).
cases.remark: Append-only TD queue; stateless subroutine; CICS serialises TD WRITEQ — idempotent per call

cases.mid: 連携・インターフェース (Linkage / interface)
cases.name: CICS LINK contract — the handler reads a 126-byte parameter area by position and never returns normally
cases.precondition: F-STD. The caller passes the abend-parameter area on the CICS LINK.
cases.steps:
1. The caller invokes the handler by CICS LINK, passing the 126-byte parameter area (layout in Test data)
2. Observe which bytes the handler consumes
3. Observe whether control returns to the caller's next statement
cases.data: Layout (126 bytes): program bytes 1-8, paragraph 9-38, response code 39-42, reason code 43-46, detail 47-126. F-STD values.
cases.expected: The handler consumes the program (bytes 1-8), paragraph (9-38) and detail (47-126) from the supplied area and ignores the response/reason bytes (39-46). Because the handler abends the task, control does NOT return to the caller's next statement — the abend propagates to the caller's abend handler or terminates the task.
cases.remark: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING KABND-PARM (COPY KABND, 126 bytes) · EXEC CICS ABEND precedes GOBACK ⇒ GOBACK (L40) unreachable, no RETURN to caller

cases.mid: メッセージ・異常系 (Messages / abnormal)
cases.name: Task is abended with code OABN and a transaction dump
cases.precondition: F-STD. The caller has invoked the handler after a failure.
cases.steps:
1. Invoke the handler under F-STD
2. Observe the task's abend code and whether a dump is produced
3. Confirm the task does not continue
cases.data: Fixed abend code = OABN (constant). F-STD inputs.
cases.expected: The task is terminated by a CICS ABEND with code OABN and the default transaction dump is taken. The failing task ends abnormally and does not resume; the ABEND code is always the constant OABN irrespective of the input values.
cases.remark: EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE(WS-ABCODE) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) · WS-ABCODE VALUE 'OABN' · dump is the ABEND default · L36-39

cases.mid: メッセージ・異常系 (Messages / abnormal)
cases.name: Log queue not defined — the write fails silently and the task still abends, losing the line
cases.precondition: F-STD, except the CICS log queue CSSL is not defined in the region.
cases.steps:
1. Omit / remove the CSSL queue definition
2. Invoke the handler under F-STD
3. Observe the write result, the CSSL queue, and the task outcome
cases.data: CSSL undefined → write returns QIDERR (response 16). F-STD inputs. Expected: no line logged; task abends with OABN.
cases.expected: The write to the CSSL queue returns a QIDERR response, but the handler does not test the response, so it proceeds to ABEND the task with code OABN. No diagnostic line is captured — the failure still triggers the CICS ABEND but the audit line is lost.
cases.remark: RESP(WS-RESP-CD) captured on WRITEQ TD but never tested (no branch) — design §5.2 'response check' has no counterpart in source; this env fault exercises the unchecked-RESP path

cases.name: Minimal input — all text fields blank still produces a 120-byte line and abends
cases.precondition: F-STD, except program, paragraph and detail are all spaces (blank).
cases.steps:
1. Invoke the handler with all three text fields set to spaces
2. Read the CSSL line and its length
3. Observe the task outcome
cases.data: program=8 spaces, paragraph=30 spaces, detail=80 spaces. Expected line: 'ABEND IN ' + 8 spaces + ' AT ' + 30 spaces + ' - ' + spaces; total 120 bytes.
cases.expected: A 120-byte line is still written: the fixed labels 'ABEND IN ', ' AT ', ' - ' surrounded by spaces where the values were blank. The task still abends with code OABN. No error is raised for empty input — the handler requires no field to be present.
cases.remark: STRING with DELIMITED SIZE copies full field width even when spaces — min-side boundary · L22-29

cases.name: Detail fills the line exactly to 120 bytes — the whole line is preserved with no loss
cases.precondition: F-STD, except the detail's significant text occupies exactly its first 66 bytes (positions 67-80 are spaces).
cases.steps:
1. Supply a detail whose significant text is 66 characters, positions 67-80 spaces (see Test data)
2. Read the CSSL line
3. Confirm no significant characters are dropped
cases.data: Fixed prefix = 54 bytes (labels 16 + program 8 + paragraph 30); 54 + 66 = 120. detail significant 66 chars, e.g. 'ACCOUNT MASTER UPDATE FAILED - FILE STATUS 23 ON ACCTFILE KEY 001'.
cases.expected: The assembled line is exactly 120 bytes and every significant character of the detail is preserved — the 14 bytes dropped by the 120-byte buffer are the detail's trailing spaces (positions 67-80), so no information is lost. The task abends with code OABN.
cases.remark: labels 16 + program 8 + paragraph 30 = 54 fixed; leaves 66 bytes for detail within the 120-byte buffer — boundary where content just fits

cases.name: Full-width input overflows the 120-byte buffer — the tail of the detail is truncated
cases.precondition: F-STD, except every text field is filled to its maximum (program 8, paragraph 30, detail 80 significant characters).
cases.steps:
1. Supply program, paragraph and detail all at full width (see Test data)
2. Read the CSSL line and compare it against the input detail
3. Observe the task outcome
cases.data: program=8 chars, paragraph=30 chars, detail=80 significant chars. Assembled = 16 + 8 + 30 + 80 = 134 bytes > 120 buffer. Detail bytes 67-80 (last 14) dropped from the line.
cases.expected: The assembled text is 134 bytes but the line buffer holds only 120, and there is no overflow handling, so the buffer silently truncates: only the first 66 bytes of the 80-byte detail reach the CSSL line; detail bytes 67-80 are lost. The task still abends with code OABN — truncation does not stop processing.
cases.remark: STRING (no ON OVERFLOW) into WS-ABEND-MSG X(120); 'ABEND IN '(9)+program(8)+' AT '(4)+paragraph(30)+' - '(3)=54, +66/80 detail = 120 — max-plus boundary · L22-29
